subject: AtlasFin on-prem deployment — readiness checklist & network gating
body:
From: Lucas Chen <lucas.chen@atlasfin.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@atlasfin.com
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial ask — AtlasFin on-prem deployment needs

Hi Karthik / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're planning an on-prem rollout for a subset of Redwood inference endpoints inside our PCI-scoped K8s clusters. Before we lock timelines, our infra and security teams need a short readiness check from Redwood covering:

- Minimum cluster sizing and recommended node pool split (control plane vs workers, GPU vs CPU).
- Storage profile: PVC classes, RWX vs RWO guidance for model cache and persistence.
- Network requirements: egress rules, firewall ports, and service-to-service subnet mapping.
- Authentication/identity: connections to our IdP and any certificate transfer process.

Can you send a concise checklist we can validate with our platform team? Ideally by Monday 4/13. Also attaching the baseline k8s version and our current node types.

Thanks,
Lucas

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Initial ask — AtlasFin on-prem deployment needs

Lucas — appreciate the clear list. I've put together a short readiness checklist below and attached our baseline RFC and a sizing spreadsheet that maps to your node types. If anything is unclear we can jump on a 30-min tech sync.

Redwood on-prem readiness checklist (high level):

1) Cluster baseline
   - Kubernetes: 1.25+ supported. We recommend 1.26 for CSI/sidecar compatibility.
   - Control plane: high-availability recommended for production (3 masters).

2) Node pools
   - GPU pool(s): NVIDIA A10/A30/A100 variants supported. Recommend dedicated GPU nodes for model inference (no user pods).
   - CPU pool(s): Separate for sidecars, routers, autoscaler components. Preferred instance types to match your baseline (we matched your inventory in the sheet).
   - Node sizing: initial suggestion in attached atlasfin-nodepool-sizing.xlsx; typical ratio 1:3 (GPU:CPU) depending on expected concurrency.

3) Storage
   - Model cache: RWO PVC per GPU node (fast NVMe-backed). Mounts should allow >200GB per GPU node for medium models.
   - Shared artifacts: RWX (NFS/CSI) for shared config and logs if needed — use access controls and encryption at rest.
   - Backups: periodic snapshotting of stateful volumes; we include retention guidelines in the RFC.

4) Networking
   - Ports: outbound HTTPS (443) for telemetry & optional model pull; inter-node gRPC/TCP ranges (configured in RFC). Avoid opening wide CIDR ranges.
   - Egress gating: allow connections to our registry endpoints and control plane IPs.
   - Service mesh: supported but we recommend bypassing sidecar for high-throughput inference paths or using mTLS with passthrough.

5) Security & identity
   - Certificates: we support either customer-provided certs (K8s secrets) or Redwood-signed cert bundles delivered via secure transfer.
   - IdP: SAML/OIDC integrations supported for console/auth flows; service accounts used for node-to-control-plane auth.

6) Ops & observability
   - Metrics: Prometheus scrape targets and Grafana dashboards included in RFC.
   - Tracing: optional jaeger collector for request tracing.

Next steps / asks for AtlasFin
- Confirm target k8s minor version and cluster HA requirements.
- Provide a reachable CIDR and baseline firewall policy.
- Confirm whether model pull must happen over private peering or via egress.

Attachments: atlasfin-nodepool-sizing.xlsx, redwood-onprem-rfc-v1.2.pdf, atlasfin-firewall-rules.csv

—
Karthik Iyer
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192


On Mon, Apr 12, 2026 at 09:45:12 -0700 Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks — adding a few technical specifics for the platform team.
>
> Hi Lucas / AtlasFin ops,
>
> Quick clarifications from the runtime side:
>
> - Node kernel params: we require net.core.somaxconn=1024 and vm.max_map_count >= 262144 for large KV caches. If you run Calico, annotate the GPU nodes to skip hostendpoint policy for performance.
>
> - Storage class guidance: use a CSI driver that exposes volumeTopology (zone-aware) for fast local mounts. For NVMe-backed local volumes we prefer local persistent volumes with nodeAffinity to ensure model locality.
>
> - Networking rules (minimal):
>   * Allow outbound to registry.redwood.ai:443 and telemetry.redwood.ai:443
>   * Allow inter-node TCP range 30000-32767 for ephemeral ports and 50000-50050 for gRPC pooling
>
> - Autoscaling: we support KEDA for queue-based scaling; configure a conservative cooldown (2–3 min) to avoid thrash.
>
> I'll be on the sync if we need to dig into kubelet configs and the CSI profile.
>
> Cheers,
> Dev
> Senior SWE, Runtime — Redwood Inference
> dev_patel@redwood.com

Lucas — from a commercial / timeline perspective:

- We can support a limited pilot in 4–6 weeks after signoff (assuming access & cert exchange).
- For Dedicated on-prem licensing, we'll need a short SOW and a procurement contact — looping in procurement@atlasfin.com.
- There may be a brief window to request an exception for earlier delivery if you can commit to a staging window and provide an engineer on your side for initial pairing.

Please let us know your procurement timeline and the names of the AtlasFin engineers who will do hands-on pairing.
